title: さっき — a little while ago
summary: An adverb for a short time ago, from a few minutes to a few hours. The sentence usually ends in the past tense. For polite speech, use 先ほど.

patterns.gloss: さっき + past tense (さっき電話があった)
さっきまで + ～ていた (until a moment ago)

body.p: さっき refers to a moment just before now. Unlike 昨日 or 先週, it is not a fixed point but a feeling of “just a bit ago”.
It is normally used in past-tense sentences. さっきまで shows a state that continued until a moment ago and is different now. In polite or business situations use 先ほど.

examples.ja: さっき田中（たなか）さんから電話（でんわ）がありました。
examples.romaji: Sakki Tanaka-san kara denwa ga arimashita.
examples.tr: There was a call from Mr. Tanaka just now.

examples.ja: さっき食（た）べたばかりなのに、もうお腹（なか）がすいた。
examples.romaji: Sakki tabeta bakari na noni, mō onaka ga suita.
examples.tr: Even though I ate just a little while ago, I'm already hungry.

examples.ja: さっきまで晴（は）れていたのに、急（きゅう）に雨（あめ）が降（ふ）ってきた。
examples.romaji: Sakki made harete ita noni, kyū ni ame ga futte kita.
examples.tr: It was sunny until a little while ago, but it suddenly started to rain.

pitfalls: Do not use it for the future (× さっき行きます).
Use 先ほど with superiors or in business.
